findings.title: remove() can throw NPE when the alias does not exist, breaking removal of non-existent IDPs
findings.body: In remove(String alias), the code now unconditionally calls idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) and stores the result in storedIdp, then later passes storedIdp to registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) and registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp). If no IDP with the given alias exists, getByAlias returns null, and registerIDPInvalidation(null) dereferences idp.getInternalId() (line 366), throwing a NullPointerException. Previously the code had the same latent issue in the isInvalid branch (registerIDPInvalidation(idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias))), but the new code extends the null dereference to the common path: registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) calls getLoginPredicate().test(idp), which starts with Objects::nonNull so it tolerates null, but registerIDPInvalidation does not. The contract of remove() is to return false when the IDP is not found (per the interface javadoc: 'true if an IDP with the specified alias was found and removed; false otherwise'), so callers expect a boolean, not an exception. Consequence: removing a non-existent IDP alias (e.g. via admin REST DELETE on a missing alias, or cleanup code) now throws NPE instead of returning false, and the subsequent idpDelegate.remove(alias) is never reached.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate now depends on OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC config, changing semantics for all callers and breaking non-organization deployments
findings.body: The getLoginPredicate() static method was changed to include '.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))'. This predicate is used in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.registerIDPLoginInvalidation and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate to decide whether an IDP qualifies as a login IDP. The predicate now references OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC, which is an organization-feature concept. In deployments where the ORGANIZATION feature is disabled, org-linked IDPs should not exist, so the predicate's organizationId==null branch covers them. However, the predicate calls idp.getConfig().get(...) without null-checking the config map — if an IdentityProviderModel has a null config (possible for newly constructed models before config initialization, or in tests), this throws NPE. More importantly, the predicate's semantics changed: previously it only checked ENABLED, LINK_ONLY, HIDE_ON_LOGIN; now it also requires BROKER_PUBLIC=true for org-linked IDPs. This is used to decide cache invalidation — if an org-linked IDP has BROKER_PUBLIC=false, it's not considered a login IDP, so create/update/remove of such IDPs won't invalidate the login caches. But the default getForLogin implementation (lines 165-184) uses getLoginSearchOptions() which does NOT include the BROKER_PUBLIC filter for REALM_ONLY mode (it sets ORGANIZATION_ID=null), and for ORG_ONLY/ALL it adds BROKER_PUBLIC=true to search options. So the predicate and the actual query are now consistent for org-linked IDPs. However, the predicate is a public static API (getLoginPredicate) that other code may call; changing its semantics is a contract break for any external caller expecting the old behavior (enabled && !linkOnly && !hideOnLogin).

findings.title: Inconsistent isEnabled re-check: ORG_ONLY branch with organization uses organization.getIdentityProviders() without BROKER_PUBLIC re-check on wrapped models
findings.body: In searchForIdentityProviders, the onlyOrganizationBrokers branch when this.organization != null (line 66) uses organization.getIdentityProviders() and filters with 'idp.isEnabled() && !idp.isLinkOnly() && !idp.isHideOnLogin() && Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))'. The isEnabled() here may be the wrapped version from createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (which checks org enabled state). However, the ORG_ONLY branch when organization == null (line 74) and the ALL branch (line 79) now re-check idp.isEnabled() after getForLogin, with the comment 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped'. But the organization != null branch (line 66) does NOT re-check isEnabled() after organization.getIdentityProviders() — it checks it inline in the filter, which is fine. The inconsistency is that the ALL branch (line 79-82) filters with idp.isEnabled() but does NOT filter on BROKER_PUBLIC or link-only/hide-on-login again, relying on getForLogin to have filtered correctly. Since getForLogin now caches results and the cache may contain IDPs whose BROKER_PUBLIC was true at cache time but the org was later disabled, the wrapper's isEnabled() returns false and they're filtered out — OK. But if BROKER_PUBLIC is flipped false→true on an org-linked IDP without invalidating the login cache (the gap described in the registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate finding), getForLogin(ALL, orgId) would not include the newly-public IDP, and the bean would not show it. The re-check of isEnabled() is a partial mitigation but doesn't cover the BROKER_PUBLIC staleness.

findings.title: Test cleanup uses wrong alias 'alias' instead of the actual created alias, leaking test IDPs
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin, IDPs are created with aliases 'idp-alias-0' through 'idp-alias-20' (lines 372-382 and 418-425), but the cleanup registration at lines 381 and 425 uses 'getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)' — the literal string "alias", not the actual alias variable. This means the cleanup will attempt to remove an IDP with alias "alias" which doesn't exist, and all 21 created IDPs ('idp-alias-0' to 'idp-alias-20') are leaked into the test realm. The same bug exists in testCacheIDPByOrg at line 303. Consequence: test pollution — leaked IDPs persist across test methods in the same realm, potentially affecting other tests that count IDPs or iterate over all IDPs (e.g. tests that assert on the number of identity providers in the realm, or login page tests that render all IDPs). This can cause flaky failures in subsequent tests and makes the test suite non-hermetic.

findings.title: testCacheIDPForLogin assumes organizations().getAll() ordering to pick orgaId, making the test fragile
findings.body: Line 384: 'String orgaId = testRealm().organizations().getAll().get(0).getId();' assumes the first organization returned by getAll() is 'orga' (created in onBefore at line 59). The test then associates IDPs 10-19 with this org and asserts specific counts (e.g. line 409: assertEquals(5, identityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(orgaId).size())). If getAll() returns organizations in a different order (e.g. by ID which is UUID-based and random, or by name), get(0) could be 'orgb' instead of 'orga', causing the IDP associations to go to the wrong org and all subsequent count assertions to fail. The test does not verify which organization it got — it should look up the org by domain name (e.g. testRealm().organizations().getByDomainName("orga.org") or similar) or by the known name 'orga'. This makes the test non-deterministic and likely to fail intermittently depending on UUID ordering or database return order.

findings.title: Test removes 'idp-alias-1' but never verifies the removal effect on cached login results
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin step 1 (lines 417-440), the test creates 'idp-alias-20' (hideOnLogin=true, not a login IDP) and removes 'idp-alias-1' (which was disabled, i%2==0 for i=1 is false, so enabled=false — not a login IDP). The test then asserts that all login caches still exist (lines 435-439). However, it never verifies that the cached results are actually correct after these operations — specifically, it doesn't re-run getForLogin and check the returned IDP count or contents. Since 'idp-alias-1' was disabled (not in any login cache), its removal correctly doesn't invalidate caches, but the test doesn't confirm the caches still return the right data. More importantly, the test doesn't cover the case of removing an IDP that IS in the login cache (e.g. removing 'idp-alias-0' which is enabled and realm-level), which should invalidate the caches via registerIDPLoginInvalidation. The remove() path's invalidation logic for login caches is only tested indirectly; a direct test of removing a login-eligible IDP and verifying cache invalidation is missing.

findings.title: update() calls getById() which may return null, causing NPE in registerIDPInvalidation and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate
findings.body: In update(IdentityProviderModel model), line 91: 'IdentityProviderModel idpById = getById(model.getInternalId());' — if no IDP exists with the given internalId, getById returns null (line 124: 'if (internalId == null) return null;' and line 134: 'if (model == null) return null;'). The result is then passed to registerIDPInvalidation(idpById) at line 92, which dereferences idp.getInternalId() (line 366) → NPE. It's also passed to registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model) at line 93, which calls getLoginPredicate().test(original) — the predicate starts with Objects::nonNull so it handles null original gracefully (returns false), but then the logic proceeds: !test(null)=true && !test(updated) — if updated is also not a login IDP, returns early; otherwise falls through to invalidate. So registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate tolerates null original, but registerIDPInvalidation does not. The consequence: calling update() on a non-existent internalId throws NPE instead of either silently succeeding or throwing a meaningful exception. The JPA delegate's update would likely throw its own exception for a non-existent ID, but the NPE happens before reaching the delegate, masking the real error and potentially leaving the transaction in an inconsistent state.
